# Managed block — what gets injected into the user's main instruction file

The installer adds a **delimited block** to the user's primary instruction file (`CLAUDE.md` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md` / `AGENTS.md`) that **references** the passive context skill. The block is idempotent: re-running install just replaces the existing block; uninstall removes it cleanly without touching anything else.

## Delimiters (literal)

The block is always wrapped in these two lines, **including the leading `<!--`**:

```
<!-- BEGIN unreal-agent (managed — do not edit; regenerated by install/AGENT-INSTALL.md) -->
…content…
<!-- END unreal-agent -->
```

Anything outside the delimiters is the user's content and must not be modified.

## Content variant per harness

### Claude Code — block injected into `CLAUDE.md`

```markdown
<!-- BEGIN unreal-agent (managed — do not edit; regenerated by install/AGENT-INSTALL.md) -->
## Unreal Agent — passive context skill

This project has the `unreal-agent` MCP server connected. A passive context skill at
[`.claude/skills/unreal-agent/SKILL.md`](.claude/skills/unreal-agent/SKILL.md) teaches the agent how to use it.

**Trigger:** for ANY task touching this UE5 project — analyzing a bug, observing
editor/scene/runtime state, reading or editing Blueprints / materials / animation /
widgets / levels, spawning actors, running PIE, screenshots — prefer the
`unreal-agent` MCP tools over guessing from source files.

**Precedence:** the rest of this file (and every other instruction in this project)
takes precedence over the skill. The skill only adds UE5 know-how.

Full catalog of ~187 tools: [`.claude/skills/unreal-agent/TOOLS.md`](.claude/skills/unreal-agent/TOOLS.md).
Canonical flows: [`.claude/skills/unreal-agent/FLOWS.md`](.claude/skills/unreal-agent/FLOWS.md).
<!-- END unreal-agent -->
```

## Injection algorithm (for the installer to follow)

```pseudo
target = path to CLAUDE.md | copilot-instructions.md | AGENTS.md
contents = read(target) or ""

beginMarker = "<!-- BEGIN unreal-agent"
endMarker   = "<!-- END unreal-agent -->"

if both markers present:
    replace the region between (and including) them with the new managed block
else:
    append a blank line + the new managed block to the end of the file
```

## Uninstall algorithm

```pseudo
if both markers present in target:
    remove the region between (and including) them
    if the only thing left is whitespace, remove the file (only if installer created it)
```

## Why a delimited block (and not a separate file)

A separate file the user doesn't `@`-include doesn't get loaded. The delimited block ensures the skill is **always visible** to the harness in its primary instruction file, while staying surgically replaceable. The block stays tiny — the content lives in the referenced skill files — so the user can read it and accept it at a glance.
